# Hopperlace

> Choose AI for what you want to do — and what matters to you.

We're developing independent, hands-on comparisons of AI tools: testing them on the same tasks, checking their outputs, and recording the effort needed to get a usable result.

ValueCompass, which you can use today, adds research on the companies behind those tools: their ownership, dependencies and policies.

The aim is to bring these comparisons together with ValueCompass, so you can consider practical fit and values in the same decision.

Focus: independent testing · comparison · informed choice.

## Two parts of one decision

- Tool testing (in development): can it do your task, and what will it take? Find out which tools suit a particular task, and what effort, expertise and compromises each one involves.
- ValueCompass (live, https://valuecompass.ai): who is behind it, and does that fit your values? Compare AI options on ownership, control and documented commitments, against the priorities you choose.

## Tool testing — in development

See how AI tools perform on the work you need done.

Our comparisons are meant to show which tools fit your work and circumstances, and what you'd be taking on with each.

To get there, several tools receive comparable tasks, each task is run more than once, and we check the outputs independently rather than relying on what the tool reports.

Our first comparisons will focus on AI app builders.

### Example test scenario: building and maintaining a booking app

- Decision: which AI app builder suits a small-business owner with limited technical experience?
- Evaluation scope:
  - Functional reliability — booking and cancellation flows, including attempts to reserve the same slot.
  - Maintainability — introducing a new requirement and checking that existing functionality still works.
  - User effort — time, correction attempts and technical assistance needed to complete the task.
  - Portability — exporting the project and assessing what is required to run it with another provider.
- Intended outcome: a comparison of which tools suit this user, where specialist help is needed, and the trade-offs involved.

### What we'll record

1. Does it work? — whether the output does what the task asked.
2. Fixes — what errors occur, and how many attempts it takes to resolve them.
3. Time — from the initial instructions to a usable result.
4. Cost — what it costs to complete the task, including retries.
5. Assistance — the guidance and technical knowledge needed to reach a useful result.

### What you'll get

- Options worth trying for your kind of task.
- The circumstances in which each tool struggles.
- The effort and expertise you should expect to contribute.
- The evidence behind the advice, including example outputs.
- The trade-offs that could change the recommendation.

Note: this describes planned testing, not published results. No comparisons have been published yet.

## ValueCompass — available now (https://valuecompass.ai)

Explore the values behind your AI choices.

Who benefits from the money you spend on AI? What commitments do providers make to the people affected by their technology?

ValueCompass helps you examine the companies behind AI products and compare options against your values. Explore ownership, control, dependencies and documented policies, with sources and clear gaps in the research.

Opens valuecompass.ai. No account needed.

## Founder

Hopperlace was founded by Yuyu Shen, a statistically trained data scientist turned product manager with nearly a decade building and evaluating AI systems, including taking AI products from zero to one.

She also built Evidence Synthesis AI (https://www.evidencesynthesisai.com/), which helps research teams use AI to screen studies for systematic reviews. Her research on deference-aware evaluation was accepted at the ICML 2026 Technical AI Governance workshop. She holds CCA-F and CCA-P certifications and writes about technology, agency and better decisions at https://buildwithwhy.com.

## Services (https://hopperlace.ai/services)

Develop, test and improve AI products and features.

Hopperlace helps teams turn promising ideas into working prototypes, find out what is holding existing AI experiences back, and use evidence to decide what to build or change next.

### 01 / A new idea: develop and test an AI idea

"We see an opportunity for AI in our product or workflow, but need to work out what it should do and whether it can deliver."

The work can include:

1. Understand the user's task and how it is done today.
2. Define what a useful result would look like.
3. Explore suitable tools, models and system designs, including whether to build or buy.
4. Build a focused, working prototype.
5. Test it on cases that reflect real use.
6. Explain what works, what remains uncertain, and the next development step.

You receive: a working prototype, findings from testing, and a practical recommendation for what to develop next.

### 02 / An existing feature: improve an existing AI experience

"The demo looks promising, but real users still struggle, correct the output, or redo the work."

The work can include:

1. Review real examples and where users run into trouble.
2. Agree what success should mean for the people using it.
3. Trace the problem across model behavior, the information the system has, the workflow and the interface.
4. Prototype or implement selected improvements.
5. Compare results before and after on the same set of cases.
6. Hand over test cases your team can rerun, and clear next steps.

You receive: a diagnosis supported by real examples, tested changes where agreed, and evidence of their effect.

### 03 / What a project can look like (illustrative example)

A team wants to help customers turn a collection of documents into an actionable plan.

1. Understand the task — which documents customers start with, what the plan needs to help them decide, and what a good plan looks like to them.
2. Prototype the experience — a working version that reads a realistic set of documents and drafts a plan customers can review and edit.
3. Test the plans — run it on representative document sets and check each plan: is it accurate, complete, and something a customer could act on?
4. Find the review points — where plans tend to need correcting, and where a person should check before anything is acted on.
5. Recommend the next step — what to build next, what to change, and which questions to answer before offering it more widely.

### 04 / How projects work

Focused, hands-on, and set up for your team to carry on.

1. An agreed question — each project starts with the question it needs to answer, a scope, and the outputs you'll receive.
2. Hands-on work — discovery, prototyping, testing and selected implementation, in whatever mix the question calls for.
3. A clear handoff — prototype, tests and findings are handed over so your team can continue the development.

What the work draws on: customer and workflow discovery · AI product and interaction design · tool, model and build-versus-buy decisions · system architecture, including where people stay involved · functional prototyping and selected implementation · designing tests and interpreting the results.

### 05 / Who you'll be working with: Yuyu Shen, founder

Yuyu is a statistically trained data scientist turned product leader, with nearly a decade building and evaluating AI systems, including taking AI products from zero to one.

Her work has always sat between the technical and the commercial. She builds models and prototypes herself, then turns what they show into product decisions, keeping both tied to what customers actually need. That combination is what she brings to a project: judgment about what is worth building, the ability to build and measure it, and attention to how people will really use it.

She now builds independently through Hopperlace. That includes ValueCompass (https://valuecompass.ai), for comparing AI options against your values, and Evidence Synthesis AI (https://www.evidencesynthesisai.com/), which helps research teams use AI to screen studies for systematic reviews. Alongside building, she researches how AI systems should be evaluated and writes about technology, agency and better decisions.

- Research: deference-aware evaluation. Paper accepted at the ICML 2026 Technical AI Governance workshop.
- Certifications: CCA-F (Certified Claude Architect – Foundational); CCA-P (Certified Claude Architect – Professional).
- Writing: Build With Why (https://buildwithwhy.com), essays on technology, agency and better decisions.

Selected experience from previous roles (not Hopperlace client projects):

- Enjoy Technology — Last Mile Smart Routing. Personally built a Python proof-of-concept algorithm for adaptive delivery coverage, then led the work into product development. The feature increased visits per vehicle by 8–13%.
- Beamery — Dynamic Job Architecture. As hiring slowed, identified an opportunity to adapt Beamery's existing AI capabilities into Dynamic Job Architecture; persuaded leadership to explore the area, secured support for a team and found willing pilot customers. The work extended Beamery's capabilities toward defining roles and skills for internal mobility and workforce planning.

### 06 / Why Hopperlace

The same questions behind our product work. Client projects and Hopperlace's public tool testing, now in development, start from the same questions: what an AI system actually accomplishes, where it struggles, and what makes it right for a particular task and person. Client work stays confidential.
